THREE ORDER DEFECTS, FOUR TOOL ITEMS FOR T26, TWO HARNESS TRAPS REPRODUCED, AND ONE ERROR OF THIS LANE'S OWN.

ORDER DEFECT 1 -- A CITATION THAT DOES NOT RESOLVE. The charter names its own source record as `attempt.CU_addr16-live-zero-law-reconciliation-...20260904.v1`, with a literal ellipsis. `python memory_graph/gdlmem.py record attempt.CU_addr16-live-zero-law-reconciliation-...20260904.v1` returns `gdlmem: error: no record with id '...'`; the real id is attempt.CU_addr16-live-zero-law-reconciliation-four-contradictions-and-every-roster-number-in-the-family-is-stale-at-head.20260904.v1 and it took a `gdlmem search` to recover. AGENTS.md's dispatch screen 'Citations resolve to record ids' is written for exactly this. Cost was small (one query) but the failure mode is not: an elided id is indistinguishable from a typo'd one, and a lane that guessed instead of searching would have worked from the wrong record.

ORDER DEFECT 2 -- A ROW COUNT STALE BEFORE THE LANE STARTED. The charter says 'disposition the 14 CROSS-LANE CITED rows'. At HEAD `python tools/gdl/composed_census/t25_falsifier_freshness.py` prints `CITED rows (high confidence) : 37 = 15 CROSS-LANE + 22 same-lane`. The fifteenth is claim.law.CR_mwcc-epilogue-restore-order...v1 / attempt.WS_critterdamageplayer-refused-the-epilogue-window...20260904.v1, whose attempt is stamped 2026-09-04T14:58:18Z -- after the 14:44:12Z record the order was written from. A count in an order is a present-tense number and needs re-measuring, which is already the rule; this is that rule paying for itself on a 14-hour-old order.

ORDER DEFECT 3 -- THE CHANGED-UNIT SET WAS FOUR OF SEVEN WRONG, AND THE NEW RULE CAUGHT IT ON ITS FIRST RUN. The charter names 'mb_camera, critter, ml_mem, gamemain, pb_error, auxanim, enemy' as the run-55 changed units. `git diff --name-only 9052e0eda..670e7efac -- src/` returns exactly `src/game/game/gamemain.c`, `src/game/pb/pb_error.c`, `src/game/sys/ml_mem.c`, and the same three come back from both alternative range boundaries. The other four last changed in run 54 or earlier -- `git merge-base --is-ancestor <c> 9052e0eda` exits 0 for mb_camera's 39128d179, critter's 9add83c16, auxanim's a19fb90ba and enemy's cdf25509e. The rule that a record must CARRY the git command producing its changed-unit set earned itself on its first application: executed as written, the sweep would have spent most of its checks on units run 55 never touched.

TOOL ITEMS FOR T26, all four on tools T25 shipped or owns. (1) `t25_record_recheck.py` HAS NO CORPUS MODE but its docstring's headline calibration is a corpus figure ('347 HELD ... 8 read STALE', measured 030385209, 'run in-process over the whole corpus'). `--help` takes one positional `record`, so that number is unreachable from any shipped command and cannot be re-derived by the lane the tool is written for. A driver over its own advertised IMPORTABLE CORE reads 121 STALE / 384 HELD over 546 re-checkable records at HEAD. Ship `--corpus`. (2) `t25_falsifier_freshness.py`'s CITED tier NEEDS A VERB DISCRIMINATOR: 13 of its 15 cross-lane rows are records CITING the law as compliance (the literal words are SCREENED / APPLIED / HONOURED / CONFIRMED / 'SCREENED and NOT applicable'), not contradicting it, so its highest-confidence tier is 87% benign for a custodial consumer. Classify on the verb adjacent to the law id and print two tiers. (3) STALE SHOULD SPLIT ON WHETHER A RECORD ANCHORS ITS NUMBERS TO A COMMIT -- 85 of the 121 already do, satisfying the tool's own stated alternative remedy ('or say which commit each number belongs to'), leaving 36 as the actionable set. (4) `gdlmem stale`'s rows CARRY NO `record_id`: the keys are `['function','fuzzy','record']` for stale_solved and `['function','missing_anchors','reason','record']` for reopen_candidates. Any cross-tool join keyed on record_id silently returns an empty intersection, which reads exactly like a finding -- see this lane's own error below.

A FIFTH TOOL OBSERVATION, RAISED AS A CANDIDATE AND NOT AS A BUG. `tools/gdl/addrlo_home_general_census.py` prints `TARGET shape-B in shadow: 8 not in shadow: 25` at HEAD, while claim.law.addrlo-home-copy-class-is-general-temp-and-shadow-coupled.20260901.v1 publishes 'TARGET shape-B in shadow 2/33' -- same denominator, different numerator, on the side that CANNOT move, since the target is the dtk-split retail image. `git log --oneline -- tools/gdl/addrlo_home_general_census.py` returns exactly one commit (3eb63a60b), so the tool has never been edited, and its printing loop reads only the target store. The contrast that makes this worth a look: the SIBLING tool's target-side numbers reproduce v1's exactly (IN_PLACE/VOL 976, FRESH/VOL 1416, FRESH/CS 920, IN_PLACE/CS 0), which is what an immutable-target number must do. This lane does NOT assert which side is wrong -- the candidates are a transcription from one of the two other tools the law's provenance names, or a pairing-set effect the code review did not catch -- and resolving it is a tool question. Recorded in claim.law.addrlo-home-copy-class-is-general-temp-and-shadow-coupled.20260901.v2.

A DENIAL-CONVENTION DEFECT, MEASURED ON 1 OF 7. attempt.GC_fn800c13cc-...20260904.v1's expiry_check names `python tools/gdl/probe.py game/pb/pb_error fn_800C13CC --ops`. probe BUILDS, and probe/defake_gate exit 3 on a unit another lane's active claim owns -- pb_error is WF's this run. A check written as a probe invocation is therefore unrunnable by a custodial sweep precisely when the unit is in flight, which is when the sweep most wants to run it. This lane substituted `fndiff --ops`, which prints the same cluster list with no build, and DECLARED the substitution in the sweep record rather than making it silently. Convention: expiry_checks name a read-only command when one decides the same question.

TWO HARNESS TRAPS REPRODUCED LIVE, BOTH ALREADY IN AGENTS.md, BOTH HIT BY A LANE THAT HAD READ THE FILE. (a) TRAP 6a: `python memory_graph/gdlmem.py propose-record <file> | Select-Object -First 3` reported `PROPOSE_EXIT=-1` while the record HAD been staged (the inbox file exists); the identical command in capture form reported `PROPOSE_EXIT=0`. That is a gate reporting a failure that did not happen, on a write-path command, which is the worst place for it. (b) DISCIPLINE 15: `python -c "..."` through the Bash tool returned `IndentationError: unexpected indent` on a line reading `||  goto :error` -- the cmd-shim injection, verbatim, on a first attempt at a two-line JSON summary. Both traps are documented, both were read at lane start, and both were still hit; the second cost one tool call, the first would have cost a false 'record failed to stage' conclusion had the inbox not been checked.

THIS LANE'S OWN ERROR, RECORDED BECAUSE THE ALTERNATIVE IS PUBLISHING IT. The first attempt at the `gdlmem stale` cross-check keyed the intersection on `record_id` and printed `overlap with my 121 STALE rows: 0` for all three buckets -- a clean, quotable, and entirely false finding, caused by tool item (4) above: those rows have no `record_id` key, so every id read None. Re-keyed on `function`, the real intersections are 2 (stale_solved), 8 (reopen_candidates) and 11 (postprocessor_walls) against 76 distinct STALE functions. A second self-caught error is recorded in the honesty-control record: the first parse of webfrank.json misread its schema and produced a void draw of three UNIT names, discarded before any function was examined.

The tool items are refuted by `t25_record_recheck.py --help` showing a corpus mode, or by reading any of the thirteen benign citing records and finding it contradicts its law rather than complying with it.
hypothesis.count_consequence: count-neutral: this lane edited no source, ran no probe, authored and deleted no rule. The project split is identical at both ends of the lane -- STRICT matched 57.20% (2594 fns) + EQUIVALENT 12.09% (160 fns), fuzzy 98.59%, matched 69.29% -- which is the expected outcome for a custodial lane and is stated so that a reader can tell a no-op from an unmeasured one.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: not applicable in the codegen sense -- this record measures orders, tools and harness behaviour, not bytes. Where it quotes a per-function number (the flip-roster blockers, the expiry-check states) that number came from fndiff/fnasm/wf_word_diff against the dtk-split retail objects under build/GUNE5D/obj/**, and those readings live in the item records rather than here.
hypothesis.statement: THE THREE ORDER DEFECTS SHARE ONE CAUSE AND ONE ONE-COMMAND FIX EACH, AND ALL THREE COMMANDS ARE ALREADY MANDATED SOMEWHERE IN AGENTS.md. An order's record citations should be pasted from `gdlmem search` output rather than abbreviated (defect 1); its present-tense counts should be re-run at dispatch rather than copied from the record that motivated the item (defect 2); and its changed-unit set should be GENERATED by the git command rather than recalled (defect 3). The next dispatch note should carry, verbatim, the three commands and their output: the full record ids, the live `t25_falsifier_freshness` header line, and `git diff --name-only <prev-accept>..<accept> -- src/`. That is roughly two minutes at dispatch against, this run, one recovered citation, one row the order did not know about, and four units of misdirected sweep.
